title: Modeled market strata and competitor trajectory brief
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: produce a defensible segmentation of the LLM market (market strata) and a 12-month competitor trajectory forecast focused on adoption risk for Redwood Inference. Scope: top 30 public/open models + top 10 closed-provider endpoints evaluated across three axes: substitution risk (how easily a customer could switch), latency/economics sensitivity (how price/latency-driven the use case is), and enterprise readiness (privacy, licensing, SLAs). Deliverables: 1) CSV scoring sheet with normalized signals, 2) 12 "trajectory cards" (one-page) for highest-risk models, 3) a one-page executive brief with recommended mitigations and triggers, 4) prioritized quick wins for product and GTM. Methodology: combine telemetry (per-route latency, model choices), sales / AE input (10 recent enterprise RFQs), public release cadence, community adoption signals (forks, Hugging Face downloads), and inferential price elasticity from synthetic workload cost runs. Outputs will drive roadmap bets (quantized variant prioritization, SLA packaging, routing policies).
acceptance_criteria: 1) CSV contains scores for at least 30 models with clear column definitions and provenance links. 2) 12 trajectory cards completed and reviewed by PM + Research. 3) Executive brief with 3 recommended mitigations and triggers accepted by Head of Product. 4) Data sources and calculation notebook shared in Drive.
comments: 2025-01-18 - Kickoff: aligned with Research and Growth; agreed signal weights (substitutability 40%, latency econ 30%, enterprise readiness 30%).
2025-01-20 - Data pull: telemetry team delivered per-route model selection counts and P50/P95 latencies for last 90 days; initial gaps in per-customer billing granularity noted.
2025-01-24 - AE interviews: summarized 8 conversations; recurring themes: latency SLAs and model explainability requests from regulated customers.
2025-01-28 - Prototype scoring: produced first CSV (30 models) using heuristic weights; flagged 6 models as 'high substitution risk'.
2025-01-30 - PM review: requested tighter signal provenance and a separate column for quantization readiness. Action: Research to run quantized inference tests on top-10 flagged models.
2025-02-03 - Quant test results uploaded: quantized 8/10 models reachable with <15% quality delta at 4-bit; added cost-per-inference estimates.
2025-02-04 - Stakeholder sync: presented draft trajectory cards to Engineering and Sales. Engineering requested two actionable tickets for kernel optimization and model-variant packaging.
2025-02-06 - Design review scheduled for 2025-02-08 to craft executive brief visuals and cut the final deliverables.
next_steps: 1) Research: finish quantization readiness columns and add quality regression metrics (due 2025-02-07). 2) Design: produce visual one-pager and 12 card templates (due 2025-02-08). 3) Eng: create two spike tickets for kernel micro-optimizations and packaging quant variants (ENG spike tickets to be created by 2025-02-06). 4) PM: finalize executive brief and distribute to Exec on 2025-02-10.
risks_and_open_questions: - Telemetry lacks per-customer spend mapping for some hosted routes, which could bias substitution scores. - Community download counts can spike on unrelated publicity events; need smoothing window. - We lack robust proprietary quality regress metrics for quantized variants; may understate quality risk.
recommended_mitigations: - Prioritize packaging a 4-bit quantized variant for the two highest-risk model families within next quarter. - Add a configurable latency SLA offering for Dedicated customers in the next sales package. - Create a lightweight buyer-facing 'model-fallback' doc for AEs to articulate fallback economics and routing behavior.
owner_notes: This brief is intended to be pragmatic and tied to measurable triggers (e.g., weekly increase in model selection for a flagged rival > 20% for 3 weeks triggers a canary test). Keep the scoring transparent so Engineering can run the same pipeline.
